sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The bucca is a household sprite of Wales. It closely resembles the brownie. The bucca would work for food. If a householder failed to leave a bowl of milk or another treat, mischief often followed. One must not ask the bucca its name. That question would make the sprite leave the farm in disgust. Some folklorists separate a helpful bucca gwidden from an evil bucca dhu. The name bucca can also serve as a plain term for a fairy.

okr.objective: Present the bucca as a Welsh household sprite that works for food and leaves when asked its name.
key_results: The bucca resembles a brownie and works for food.
